recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中紅血球在薄處仍大量疊成錢串狀排列（rouleaux），同時可見數顆中等大小、染色質較開放的單核淋巴樣細胞；「顯著錢串＋異常淋巴樣細胞」提示 IgM 單株蛋白增加的 Waldenström 巨球蛋白血症。
features: Prominent rouleaux: red cells stacked in chains in the thin area of the smear
Several medium-sized mononuclear lymphoid cells with round nuclei and more open chromatin than normal lymphocytes
Scant to moderate basophilic cytoplasm in the lymphoid cells
Bluish background staining and scattered spherocyte-like cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows prominent rouleaux formation extending into the thin, monolayer area of the smear, along with a subtle bluish background. Several medium-sized mononuclear lymphoid cells with round nuclei, a more open chromatin pattern than normal small lymphocytes, and scant to moderate basophilic cytoplasm are present. Platelets are adequate. Findings are consistent with a paraproteinemia with circulating lymphoid cells, suggestive of Waldenström macroglobulinemia/lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma; serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and flow cytometry are recommended.

ddx.vs: Myeloma also causes rouleaux, but circulating cells are plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and hofs, and the paraprotein is usually IgG/IgA rather than IgM.
Agglutinates form irregular three-dimensional clumps rather than linear coin-like stacks, and disperse on warming.
Artifactual stacking is confined to thick areas, whereas true rouleaux persists in the thin area where cells should lie separately.
CLL cells have condensed soccer-ball chromatin with smudge cells and usually no significant rouleaux.
